title: EA-CORPORA-39 — The Thirty-Ninth Seating: The Field before the Flattening — the Archiv für Geschichte der Philosophie 1888–1923, the Construction of the Object from Brucker to Lutosławski, the Philology Journals, and the Census and Gates of This Is Not Philosophy
creator: Cranes, Rebekah
description: The thirty-ninth seating of the originals shelf, thirteen seats, gathered for This Is Not Philosophy: How Disciplinarity Murdered Philosophy — The Shape of the Field, and seated before it. The Archiv für Geschichte der Philosophie I–XXXVI (1888–1923), the field before the flattening; the construction of the object: Brucker's Historia critica (1742, 1743), Hermann (1839), Zeller (1856/1865), Ueberweg (1861), Schaarschmidt (1866, with an OCR made for the seat), Grote (1865) and Lutosławski (1897); the cited volumes of Philologus and the Classical Quarterly; the census of the study, with its codes, spans, logs and scripts and without the publishers' abstracts; and the gates, as dated excerpts. Pointers to the volumes and the interim journals not seated.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Rebekah Cranes is a heteronym of Lee Sharks, the standing authority on the EA-CORPORA deposits (named by the author on 2026-11-04 and held at his word of 2026-11-05). The sources found, fetched, OCR'd where the served text layer read the scan poorly, verified, hashed and indexed, the census staged without the publishers' abstracts, the gate excerpts drawn, and the records drafted, in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction. The gathering, its object, its form and its rulings are Lee Sharks's; the scans within each seat were chosen in session and are stated per seat. CC-BY-4.0 applies to this record and the seat records.
methodology: Each seat fetched in session from the source its record names (the Internet Archive; Crossref; Persée OAI-PMH); the Archive's text layers held as served and hashed into each MANIFEST.sha256; where the served layer read the scan poorly, an OCR made from the source's page images by tesseract 5, page by page, recorded as the seat's and not corrected; the census staged by code, without the publishers' abstracts; licences read at the item; loci verified by substring with whitespace collapsed, in the scans' own readings; public-domain status checked against first publication. No text corrected by hand. The builders and this body are under rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-39/.
falsification_conditions: A seat is falsified if its files do not verify against its MANIFEST.sha256 at the canonical URL; if a verified locus is absent from the text it names; if a work is misattributed, misdated or assigned to the wrong scan; if a licence recorded for an item is not the one its source states; if a work seated as public domain is not, in the jurisdiction stated; if an OCR said to be made from a source's page images is not reproducible from them by the stated model; if any file of the census holds a publisher's abstract; if a gate excerpt is not exact to its source; or if the four surfaces (seat, index, deposit, shelf) disagree.

wiki_article: EA-CORPORA-39 is the thirty-ninth seating of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's originals shelf, deposited under Rebekah Cranes, the standing authority on the EA-CORPORA deposits, on 16 November 2026. It gathers thirteen seats for This Is Not Philosophy: How Disciplinarity Murdered Philosophy — The Shape of the Field, Lee Sharks's study of what the journals of ancient philosophy now publish, and is seated before the study, at the author's ruling, so that its analysis can be run from what is seated. The field before the flattening is the Archiv für Geschichte der Philosophie in its first thirty-six volumes, 1888–1923 (39/01), where in the 1890s about one ancient title in five puts a work's standing in question as an ordinary article: Appel on the authenticity of the Sophistes (1892), the latest athetesis of the Philebus (1896), the authenticity of the De interpretatione (1900), the order of the Metaphysics (1907/08). The construction of the object runs from Jacob Brucker's Historia critica philosophiae (1742, 1743), which narrates the ancients as systems, through Karl Friedrich Hermann's genetic reading of the dialogues (1839), Eduard Zeller's handbook, Friedrich Ueberweg on the genuineness and order of the Platonic writings (1861), Carl Schaarschmidt's athetesis (1866), seated with an OCR made for it, and George Grote's defence of the Thrasyllan canon (1865), to Wincenty Lutosławski's stylometry (1897), the instrument that fixed the received early, middle and late. The philology journals are held by the volumes the study cites: Philologus (1858–1916) and the Classical Quarterly of 1914 and 1926–1929, with the debate over the authenticity and authorship of the Hippias Major. Two seats hold the study's evidence: the census (39/12), with every figure its tables are built from — titles, DOIs, object codes, reach codes each with a verbatim span of the abstract it rests on, adjudication logs, stylometry and scripts, and the Persée metadata of the Revue philosophique de Louvain and the Revue des Études Grecques — without reseating the publishers' abstracts, which are reached by DOI; and the gates (39/13), dated excerpts of the editor's responses to the submissions at Ancient Philosophy and of the policies on AI-authored submissions at the journals and publishers where the abstract template is strongest. Schleiermacher's Platons Werke, Campbell's Sophistes and Politicus, Tennemann's System der Platonischen Philosophie and Jaeger's Aristoteles are already seated (EA-CORPORA-31 and 32) and are not reseated. The deposit points to what is held for later: three missing volumes of the Archiv, the rest of the Philologus and Classical Quarterly runs, and the open texts of the interim journals.
